issues.evidence: P16_list_tolerates_malformed_file; note_taker.py:102 read_text with no error handling -> 'UnicodeDecodeError' traceback from `list`
issues.summary: One non-UTF-8 .md file in the store makes list/show/edit/delete crash with a traceback, because every lookup goes through all_notes().
delete without -y crashes with EOFError when stdin is closed or not interactive.
Unused tempfile import, a local import inside a function, and several long lines.

issues.evidence: P13/P14/P22: new 'Meeting: "Q3" plan' --tags '#urgent,c++' writes 'title: Meeting: "Q3" plan' and 'tags: [#urgent, c++]'; yaml.safe_load raises ScannerError/ParserError
issues.summary: Titles and tags are written as unquoted plain scalars, so ordinary inputs (a colon in the title, a leading '- ', tags starting with '#') produce frontmatter that is not valid YAML, though B's own parser still reads it.

issues.evidence: P22: title '123' -> 'title: 123' is read by YAML as an int
issues.summary: Numeric-looking or boolean-looking titles change type when the file is read by a real YAML parser.
Exceptions re-raised without 'from', plus long lines.

blinding_guess.why: B ships a unit-test suite and stricter error handling (a NoteError type, reverting a failed edit, id validation), which suggests a more process-driven build, but the signal is weak.

notes: Both are single-file, stdlib-only CLIs that store notes in ~/.note-taker (probes set HOME to a temp dir) and support tag and keyword search. Interface adaptation: A's delete needs -y to skip its confirmation prompt; all other probe invocations are identical. PyYAML was used only by the probes to check that the frontmatter is valid YAML. A has a richer non-interactive edit (--title/--tags/--append), which no requirement asked for. Security is equivalent: both run the editor with shlex.split and no shell, and neither allows path traversal.
